description: Micro-tune the validated custom n=176 path from its final profile: reduce synchronization and shared-memory traffic in the 0.725 ms Householder kernel, improve occupancy or lane utilization in the 0.497 ms Sturm/inverse-iteration backtransform, and preserve all residual and portability guards.

Removed the block_sum broadcast store and second full-block barrier because both totals are consumed only by thread 0, but the build could not update cuda.cu after the root NCU capture left this worktree cache root-owned.

After restoring the NCU-owned extension cache, removing the leader-total broadcast barriers passed all 39 tests. N176 moved from parent 1239.615 to 1234.016 us (0.45% faster, within the 1% noise band); aggregate measured 46544.584 us versus parent 46511.535 due unaffected-shape noise.

Added FP32 eigen-equation and orthogonality checks at 70% of the official tolerance with whole-batch cuSOLVER fallback. All 39 fixed tests and 16 added n176 stress spectra pass; the unguarded path failed 10 of those 16. Public dense n176 stays custom and moves from 1234.016 to 1410.187 us from guard cost; aggregate is 47021.131 us.

Raised Sturm bisection from 21 to 24 iterations under the residual guard. Official validation passes; public n176 test orthogonality improved from scaled 1.52 to 0.538. Dense n176 cost rose from 1410.187 to 1420.125 us and aggregate measured 47100.409 us.

Added a fourth inverse-iteration refinement after 24-step Sturm localization. Validation passes under the guard, but public n176 test orthogonality worsened from scaled 0.538 to 2.29 and n176 runtime rose from 1420.125 to 1438.712 us. Aggregate measured 47029.991 us because unrelated n352/n2048 samples were faster.

Restored three inverse iterations and replaced explicit abs/sum/amax guard reductions with torch.linalg.matrix_norm. All tests pass; exact-commit Nsys shows reduction 720.3 us, solve 505.9 us, guard GEMMs about 32.5 us and norm kernels about 29.7 us. N176 improved to 1408.999 us and aggregate measured 46998.281 us.

Replaced the full input matrix 1-norm in the eigen residual guard with max(abs(eigenvalues)), a cheaper lower bound that makes fallback more conservative. Validation passes; public dense remains custom, n176 improved from 1408.999 to 1404.837 us, and aggregate measured 46981.366 us.

Removed the full-block barrier between disjoint trailing-matrix rank-2 updates and completed-column reflector stores, retaining the barrier before the next Householder column. Validation passes; n176 improved from 1404.837 to 1401.357 us and aggregate measured 46964.881 us.

Padded the shared eigenvector tile from stride 32 to 33 to remove four-lane row-walk bank aliasing while leaving factor storage at stride 32. Validation passes; n176 moved from 1401.357 to 1399.909 us, within noise, and aggregate measured 46949.518 us.

Stored each completed Householder reflector contiguously in transposed scratch, removed the final full shared-to-global reflector copy, and changed four-lane backtransform reads from stride-176 to contiguous. Validation passes; n176 improved from 1399.909 to 1391.053 us, aggregate measured 46957.361 us.

Split tridiagonal solve into a two-tile 128-active-thread kernel and a six-tile four-lane backtransform. Validation passes, but n176 regressed from 1391.053 to 1407.709 us; exact-commit Nsys shows solve 141.6 us plus backtransform 391.4 us versus fused 505.9 us, so phase separation adds about 27 us despite improving solve lane utilization.

Returned to the fused solve and replaced square rank-2 indexing with warp-per-row lower-triangle traversal, eliminating per-element integer division and half-square predication while preserving contiguous stores. All tests pass; n176 improves from robust fused 1391.053 to 1221.115 us (12.2%), and aggregate reaches 46487.367 us.

Explicitly cached v[row] and y[row] once per warp-row before the triangular rank-2 inner loop, avoiding alias-conservative repeated shared loads. Validation passes; n176 improves from 1221.115 to 1189.842 us (2.6%), and aggregate reaches 46361.394 us.

Hoisted the shared matrix row pointer and forced six-way unrolling of the bounded triangular column walk. Validation passes, but n176 regressed from 1189.842 to 1236.327 us and aggregate to 46513.611 us, indicating instruction/register expansion outweighs loop control savings.

Removed forced unrolling while retaining only the hoisted matrix row pointer. Validation passes; n176 returns to 1190.835 us, statistically matching the 1189.842 us parent, so the pointer hoist is neutral. Aggregate measured 46445.179 us with noisy n352/n2048 samples.

Hoisted the matrix-vector lower-row pointer in the four-lane dot path. Validation passes, but n176 regressed from 1189.842 to 1200.851 us. Exact-commit Nsys shows reduction 510.9 us and fused solve/backtransform 516.7 us; the reduction is now 29% below the original 720.3 us and solve is the largest remaining kernel.

Removed the neutral pointer experiments and reverted shared eigenvector pitch 33 to 32 while retaining coalesced transposed reflectors. Validation passes; n176 measured 1192.987 us versus padded best 1189.842 us, within noise. Aggregate measured 46417.995 us.

Reduced guarded Sturm bisection from 24 back to 21 steps. The fixed test remains well inside the guard at scaled orthogonality 1.52, all validation passes, and unsafe stress spectra still use residual fallback. N176 improves from unpadded 1192.987 to 1181.466 us; aggregate measured 46427.484 us with a noisy n352 sample.

Hoisted the invariant backtransform scale tau*dot once per reflector/eigenpair group and reused it for all updated rows. Validation passes with effectively unchanged residuals; n176 moved from 1181.466 to 1179.989 us, within noise, and aggregate measured 46443.628 us.

Replaced stride-32 shared eigenvector addressing with a 32-wide row/slot bank swizzle designed to keep both across-eigenpair and across-row accesses conflict-free. Validation passes, but address-generation overhead regresses n176 from 1179.989 to 1246.217 us and aggregate to 46546.579 us.

Reverted the regressing shared-memory swizzle and retuned the now-coalesced solver from 32 eigenpairs x 4 lanes to 16 x 8, preserving 128 threads while raising the grid from 6 to 11 tiles. All 39 tests pass; n176 improves from 1179.989 to 1103.173 us and aggregate reaches 46147.426 us. Exact Nsys shows solve/backtransform falling from 516.7 to 424.2 us while reduction remains 510.2 us.

Expanded each eigenpair group from 8 to 16 lanes, reducing pairs per block from 16 to 8 and using 22 exact-cover tiles. All 39 tests pass, but extra blocks and inactive work after short rows regress n176 from 1103.173 to 1195.073 us and aggregate to 46424.987 us; eight lanes is the better balance.

Restored the eight-lane solver and eliminated one Householder CTA barrier per column by folding y += correction*v algebraically into the symmetric rank-2 update as y_row + 2*correction*v_row. All 39 tests pass; n176 improves from 1103.173 to 1094.682 us. Aggregate measures a new 46130.862 us, though the 0.04% delta is below noise.

Had each four-lane matrix-vector group leader contribute v[row]*y[row] directly to the following block sum, using that reduction's own barrier for shared visibility and removing a separate barrier plus y reread pass. All 39 tests pass; n176 improves from 1094.682 to 1088.938 us. Aggregate is statistically unchanged at 46130.558 us.

Made every warp repeat the second-stage block reduction and retain tau/inverse/correction locally, removing two shared scalar broadcast barriers per Householder column. Validation passes, but redundant shuffle reductions and 32-way special-function work regress n176 from 1088.938 to 1109.796 us and aggregate to 46150.625 us.

Restored leader-only block reductions and changed the shared Householder matrix pitch from n+1=177 to n+4=180, mapping the eight four-lane lower-row groups onto disjoint four-bank spans. All 39 tests pass; n176 improves from 1088.938 to 1069.077 us (1.82%). Aggregate reaches 46111.508 us despite high unrelated n352/n2048 noise.

Changed reduction initialization from a full-square linear copy to a warp-per-row lower-triangle copy, since every upper read is mirrored and only the lower triangle is updated. All 39 tests pass; n176 improves modestly from 1069.077 to 1064.537 us. Aggregate measures 45949.427 us, with most of that delta coming from unrelated n352/n2048 variance.

Reduced each Householder column tail norm within one warp to remove the block-sum barrier before the scalar broadcast. Validation passes and test-seed orthogonality improves, but serializing up to six shared-load iterations regresses benchmark n176 from 1064.537 to 1152.424 us and aggregate to 46376.712 us.

Restored parallel norms and packed 32 eight-lane eigenpair groups into 256-thread blocks, reducing solver tiles per matrix from 11 to 6. All 39 tests pass, but the wider block/shared tile sharply regresses n176 from 1064.537 to 1280.374 us and aggregate to 46712.840 us; the 128-thread/16-pair geometry remains best.

Final restored measured-best content after rejecting the single-warp norm and wider solver block. Kernelguard, all 39 official tests, and 16 adversarial n176 stress families pass. Final n176 is 1064.497 us and aggregate 45998.208 us. Exact-SHA Nsys reports 468.0 us Householder reduction and 423.8 us eight-lane Sturm/inverse-iteration backtransform.

Completed 30 logged trials. Final commit fd205cd6de1de7d42e102c655580ec01ff31a748 is content-identical to measured best b9e52eef, passes 39 official plus 16 adversarial n176 cases, and benchmarks 45998.208 aggregate with n176 1064.497 us versus brief parent 46511.535/1239.615 (14.1% n176 improvement). Retained work adds conservative whole-batch residual fallback, removes redundant reduction/update barriers and traffic, uses warp-row rank updates with cached row values, stores reflectors transposed, uses 16-pair eight-lane solve tiles, aligns Householder rows at pitch 180, and loads only the lower triangle. Final profile: /home/shadeform/gpumode/autocuda/profiles/2026-07-03-13-39-25/brief-7-final-fd205cd6de1de7d42e102c655580ec01ff31a748.nsys-rep. Remaining measured openings are the now-balanced 468 us reduction and 424 us solver plus roughly 8% guard/reduction-launch overhead; single-warp norms, per-warp scalar broadcasts, 16-lane groups, 256-thread solver blocks, and shared swizzling all regressed.

Micro-tune the validated custom n=176 path from its final profile: reduce synchronization and shared-memory traffic in the 0.725 ms Householder kernel, improve occupancy or lane utilization in the 0.497 ms Sturm/inverse-iteration backtransform, and preserve all residual and portability guards.

Parallelized the fused certificate from one block per column tile to one block per 32x8 output tile with atomic column sums and a CUB block finalizer, but stock CUB on this CUDA toolchain has no cub::Max functor, so nvcc rejected the finalizer before measurement.

First fused selective certificate implementation: one tiled CUDA block per matrix/8-column group computed both eigen and orthogonality residuals, emitted per-matrix flags, and Python compacted only flagged matrices. All official and 16 stress families passed; dense flagged 0/8 while difficult spectra selectively flagged up to 8/8. N176 was 1140.658 us, aggregate 46198.542; Nsys measured the certificate at 159.4 us.

Fixed the stock-CUB max functor and completed the output-tile certificate: 32x8 blocks atomically accumulate both column norms, then one CUB block per matrix finalizes flags. All 39 tests pass; n176 improves from the first fused version's 1140.658 to 1094.939 us, aggregate 46128.804, while retaining selective repair.

Changed the certificate from 32x8 to 16x16 output tiles, halving repeated A/Qi loads across column tiles and reducing estimated global tile traffic about 39%. All 39 tests pass; n176 improves from 1094.939 to 1058.408 us, slightly below the prior PyTorch-guard endpoint, and aggregate measures 45958.726 us.

Widened the certificate to 16x32 output tiles on 512-thread blocks so each output row maps to one warp, cutting repeated global tile loads another third and removing shuffle reduction. Validation passes; n176 moves from 1058.408 to 1064.480 us and aggregate to 45965.377, a sub-1% regression.
Restore the faster 16x16 certificate output tile and pad the 16x32 shared input tile to remove half-warp row bank aliasing. Official validation 39/39 passed; full metric 46177.996, n176 1071.492 us.

Transpose certificate input tile in shared memory to avoid row-stride bank aliasing without padded addressing. Official validation 39/39 passed; full metric 46166.607, n176 1086.801 us, slower than square-tile incumbent.

Use 128-thread 16x16 certificate tiles with two output rows and four independent residual accumulators per thread to increase ILP and resident CTAs. Official validation 39/39 passed; full metric 46103.385, n176 1079.573 us, slower than 256-thread incumbent.

Compute only the upper triangle of symmetric Q^TQ-I, contributing off-diagonal magnitudes to both column sums, while retaining the full fused eigen residual. Skip lower-tile Q_i loads/FMAs. Official validation 39/39 passed; full metric 45947.306, n176 1071.452 us.

Make triangular orthogonality work block-uniform: full diagonal tiles, eigen-only lower tiles, and no lower-tile orthogonal shuffles/shared reductions. Official validation 39/39 passed; full metric 46008.413, n176 1059.793 us, recovering incumbent endpoint performance.

Specialize fused triangular certificate for fixed n176: compile-time 11x11 tile decode, 176 strides/bounds, and unrolled six inner tiles. Official validation 39/39 passed; full metric 45890.632 (suite noise outside changed shape), n176 improved to 1038.567 us from 1059.793 us.

Map certificate column tile, row tile, and matrix directly to CUDA grid x/y/z, eliminating block-index divide/modulo. Official validation 39/39 passed; full metric 45958.630, n176 1038.599 us, effectively neutral end to end.

Remove unused tridiagonal-solver info tensor, zero-fill launch, and dead zero write; solver never reported nonzero info and callers never consumed it. Official validation 39/39 passed; full metric 45885.223, n176 improved to 1029.295 us.

Skip cloning the n176 input when the blocked dense-to-band panel range is empty; the CUDA eigensolver only reads its input. Official validation 39/39 passed; full metric 45918.505, n176 improved to 1024.610 us.

Call the read-only n176 CUDA eigensolver directly from the guarded path, bypassing the now-empty generic dense-to-band wrapper. Official validation 39/39 passed; full metric 45910.969, n176 1026.137 us, neutral within measurement variance.

Stage certificate products in two exact K=88 tiles, removing tail predicates and four of six inner synchronization stages while avoiding a 32-bank row stride. Official validation 39/39 passed; full metric 45936.891, n176 1027.493 us, neutral/slightly slower than K32.

Use four exact K=44 certificate stages to retain full occupancy, eliminate tail predicates/bank-aliasing stride, and reduce barriers versus K32. Official validation 39/39 passed; full metric 45932.689, n176 1029.838 us, slower than K32.

Restore K32 and XOR-swizzle input shared tiles so half-warp row broadcasts land on distinct banks without padded-stride multiplication. Official validation 39/39 passed; full metric 45534.923 (unrelated large-shape variance), n176 regressed to 1036.384 us.

Restore unswizzled K32 staging and mark certificate input/vector/value/scratch pointers restrict to remove conservative alias dependencies in the unrolled kernel. Official validation 39/39 passed; full metric 45866.520, n176 1023.867 us, current best endpoint.

Use 16x32 certificate tiles with 256 threads and two output columns per thread, reusing input/Q_i staging across two eigenvector groups and halving CTAs while preserving triangular mirrored norm sums. Official validation 39/39 passed; full metric 45871.287, n176 improved to 1015.754 us.

Apply launch_bounds(256,7) to the 16x32 certificate after NCU showed 40-register, six-block occupancy and 44.6% no-eligible cycles. Official validation 39/39 passed; full metric 45872.793, n176 1017.139 us, slightly slower than unconstrained codegen.

Expand certificate tiles to 16x48 with three output columns per thread, increasing A/Q_i reuse and reducing the grid to four column tiles with a 32-column tail. Official validation 39/39 passed; full metric 45862.767, n176 1014.259 us, marginal endpoint improvement.

Expand certificate tiles to 16x64 with four output columns per thread; three column tiles align with the expected three-block/SM register limit and retain about three grid waves. Official validation 39/39 passed; full metric 45851.772, n176 1015.119 us, slightly slower than 16x48.

Final commit 904b07948 implements one fused CUDA eigen-residual/orthogonality certificate, per-matrix flags, and selective compacted Xsyev fallback. Official validation 39/39 and 16 adversarial n176 families all pass; flags were 0/8 on dense-cond1/lapack-even/lapack-band/random-symmetric, 1/8 on band, and 8/8 on hard families. Full metric 45851.772; n176 1015.119 us versus 1064.497 us at continuation start. Exact Nsys certificate 60.993 us (trial52) versus 159.4 us first fused and 92.1 us first tiled. Current geometry is specialized n176 16x64, K32, 256 threads; reduction/solver geometry unchanged. Profile: profiles/2026-07-03-13-39-25/brief-7-trial-52-904b07948.nsys-rep. Open directions: test 16x96 six-column reuse, device-side last-block finalization to remove the 1.9 us finalizer, or reduce the Python aggregate-flag synchronization without changing selective semantics.
